claims.head: The Mammoth should tilt the ice
claims.body: The Mammoth have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Maple Leafs near the bottom. Expect the Mammoth to spend more of the night in the Maple Leafs’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

notes.text: Kailer Yamamoto is day to day (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Michael Carcone has taken his spot beside Anders Lee and Barrett Hayton.

John Marino is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Andrew Peeke has taken his spot beside Nate Schmidt. That pair has had 55% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 72:38 together, about what it had with Marino (59%).
Kirill Marchenko is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Gavin McKenna has taken his spot beside Jack Roslovic and Auston Matthews.
Nick Blankenburg is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Dakota Mermis has taken his spot beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson.
John Tavares is out week to week (lower body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Max Domi is on long-term injured reserve and has not played this season.
Chris Tanev returned in their last game after missing 9 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Vinni Lettieri was added to the roster on Oct 19 and has played beside Colton Sissons and Gavin McKenna.
Dakota Mermis was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Oliver Ekman-Larsson.
Oliver Ekman-Larsson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 6% last season.

stakes: The Mammoth go in second in the Central with 18 points, the Maple Leafs tied for fourth in the Atlantic with 18 points.

TOR.head: A tough matchup for the Maple Leafs
TOR.body: Even though Toronto has home-ice advantage and Utah may be without Yamamoto, the Mammoth have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Toronto will be without Marchenko. The Maple Leafs can pull it off if their power play gets going.

story.head: The Mammoth should tilt the ice
paras: The Mammoth won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in Utah on Oct 13. The Mammoth (9-6-0) lost 6-3 to Philadelphia on Sunday, while the Maple Leafs (8-6-2) beat Vancouver 4-2 on Saturday. Going in, the Mammoth are second in the Central (tied for eighth in the NHL) and the Leafs sixth in the Atlantic (tied for eighth).

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.600) says: their chances are worth about .729, and their goaltending has held them back. The Maple Leafs’ record (.562) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.502), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st) and let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd). They also roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), so the Mammoth roll four lines, but the Maple Leafs lean on their top six. As for the Maple Leafs, they get their shots through better than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (31st) and have had shaky goaltending (30th). Toronto has scored 3.75 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. The Mammoth are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Maple Leafs.

Clayton Keller (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 15 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring. Logan Cooley (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with eight points in his last five games. Auston Matthews (11 G / 13 A / 24 P in 16 GP) leads the Maple Leafs in scoring and is tied for fourth in the NHL, and William Nylander (10 G / 11 A / 21 P in 16 GP) isn’t far behind.
Karel Vejmelka (6-5-0 / .868 SV% in 11 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Utah, but will likely start. Sergei Bobrovsky (3-5-2 / .885 SV% in 10 GS) is in line to start for Toronto.
The Mammoth usually control more of the chances than the Maple Leafs do.

items.text: Dylan Guenther has a point in five straight games against Toronto, with a goal in each of the last three.
The Mammoth are newly without Kailer Yamamoto, and have been without John Marino since Oct 17.

The Maple Leafs are newly without Kirill Marchenko, have been without Nick Blankenburg and John Tavares for several games, and have had to make do without Max Domi all season. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Islanders are missing more right now.
Morgan Rielly is two goals from 100.
